speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a psychiatric condition and a new movement disorder; to help me understand the connection, can you describe the specific symptoms you are experiencing and when they started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context. Since you started risperidone two months ago and your psychiatric symptoms have improved, can you describe the specific nature of this new movement disorder and whether it appears to have started after taking the medication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you describe—inner restlessness, fidgeting, and repetitive leg movements—are classic signs of akathisia. Since this began after starting risperidone, it is highly likely a side effect of the medication. Do you feel these symptoms are severe enough to interfere with your daily life, such as keeping you awake at night?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Risperidone-induced Akathisia. The clinical presentation of inner restlessness, fidgeting, and repetitive leg movements starting two months after initiating risperidone is diagnostic, and the patient's improved psychiatric status confirms the medication is the likely cause.
